topics.topic: Whether imported-section linking and record creation occur before or atomically within activation
questions: Does section linking and creation of imported plans/new PortalSections happen before activation in a separate version-building action, or atomically inside activation?
Are imported plans and linked/new PortalSection records created in a separate pre-activation action, or are they created atomically by activation?
Are imported plans and PortalSections linked and persisted before activation, or is section linking performed atomically inside activation?

quotes:
Which operation builds an imported version with its plans and
new sections, and that it must do so before activation so that operators
can re-allocate to those sections, is Q11's to design; no operator of the
running service meets this case.

- **Created by:** `budget_management` only after activation, section linking,
  previous-version deactivation, and audit commit atomically. Plans use the
  stable `(sort_order, section_id)` order; a client BudgetView is a separate
  `derived_views` projection.

In the running service no operation creates an imported budget version
(Q11, deferred), so this linking never runs; it describes the design Q11
starts from.
judgement.why: No admissible witness exists because the texts expressly say that the running product has no action that creates an imported BudgetVersion, its plans, or its sections; Q11 must first supply that missing action.

topics.topic: Initial status of a newly created ServicePrincipal
questions: What status does a newly created ServicePrincipal have?
Is a ServicePrincipal created active, created disabled, or created in a caller-selected status?

judgement.why: This is the same question about a newly created ServicePrincipal's initial status, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Initial status of a newly created ServicePrincipal
quotes: The new active `ServicePrincipal` (the route answers its safe view).
precedent.why: The later create_service_principal operation explicitly returns a newly active principal.

topics.topic: ServicePrincipal name uniqueness and its scope
questions: May two ServicePrincipal records have the same name?
May two ServicePrincipal entities have the same name, and if not, is uniqueness global or scoped by source_type?

quotes:
One public operation per State 3 capability (108), each proven by the State 4
flows `50_api_plan.json` names. An operation is what another module, the
HTTP route table or the host may call; everything else a module does is
hidden.

The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the name, the
`ProducerSourceType` and the `ProducerScopeMode`.
Access-management failures.
Writes one `ServicePrincipal` and one `AuditRecord`.
judgement.why: The closed later operation contract accepts the name as input, declares only access-management failures, and writes the principal, so equal names are permitted and have no uniqueness scope.

topics.topic: Initial status assigned to a new StaffProjectAssignment
questions: What status does `assign_staff_project` give a new StaffProjectAssignment?

quotes: The new active `StaffProjectAssignment`.
judgement.why: The later assignment operation explicitly says that the newly created assignment is active.

topics.topic: Product actions and callers allowed to read StaffProjectAssignment records directly
questions: Besides internal authorization checks, which product actions may read StaffProjectAssignment records and who may invoke them?

quotes:
One public operation per State 3 capability (108), each proven by the State 4
flows `50_api_plan.json` names. An operation is what another module, the
HTTP route table or the host may call; everything else a module does is
hidden.

IdentityInputRejected
create_staff_account
authenticate_staff
resolve_staff_session
sign_out_staff
revoke_staff_sessions
change_staff_status
change_staff_password
assign_staff_project
revoke_staff_project_assignment
perform_recovery_override
The new active `StaffProjectAssignment`.
The revoked `StaffProjectAssignment`.
judgement.why: The exhaustive later public surface has no assignment get or list action; administrators receive an assignment only from its create and revoke actions, while authorization reads remain hidden internally.

topics.topic: Product actions that directly read ServicePrincipal records
questions: Which product actions directly read ServicePrincipal records?

quotes:
One public operation per State 3 capability (108), each proven by the State 4
flows `50_api_plan.json` names. An operation is what another module, the
HTTP route table or the host may call; everything else a module does is
hidden.

create_service_principal
change_service_principal_status
issue_service_credential
revoke_service_credential
grant_producer_project
revoke_producer_project
authenticate_service_principal
authorize_producer_scope
The new active `ServicePrincipal` (the route answers its safe view).
The `ServicePrincipal` in its new status (the route answers its safe view).
judgement.why: The exhaustive later public surface defines no principal get or list action; safe principal views are returned by creation and status change, while the other listed operations read principals only as part of their own behavior.

topics.topic: Whether ServicePrincipal creation atomically creates its first credential
questions: Does creating a ServicePrincipal atomically create and return its first ServiceCredential, or can the principal exist with no credential until a separate issue action?

judgement.why: This is the same question about whether principal creation includes an initial credential, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether ServicePrincipal creation includes an initial credential and secret
quotes: Writes one `ServicePrincipal` and one `AuditRecord`.

`ServiceCredentialIssue`: the new `ServiceCredential` with the next
`key_version` and the secret in plaintext, returned once.
precedent.why: The later API makes principal creation write only the principal and audit, while the separate credential-issuance operation creates and returns the credential and one-time secret.

topics.topic: Whether credentials may be issued or rotated while a ServicePrincipal is disabled and later become usable
questions: Can an administrator issue or rotate credentials for a disabled ServicePrincipal, and if so, does such a credential become usable when the principal is re-enabled?

judgement.why: This is the same question about credential issuance for a disabled ServicePrincipal, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: ServiceCredential issuance or rotation for a disabled ServicePrincipal
quotes: `module:service_identity`. Issue a new bearer credential for an active service principal.
precedent.why: The later operation permits issuance only for an active ServicePrincipal and generates nothing for a disabled one.

topics.topic: Whether grants may be managed for an all-projects ServicePrincipal
questions: May an administrator create or revoke ProducerProjectGrant records for a ServicePrincipal whose immutable `scope_mode` is `all_projects`?

judgement.why: This is the same question about creating producer grants for an all-projects principal, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether all-projects principals may receive ProducerProjectGrants
quotes:
### Errors

Access-management failures; `ScopedNotFoundError` for a project the Registry
does not know or an unknown principal; `ArchivedProjectRejected` for an
inactive project; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant;
`RegistryBoundaryError`.
precedent.why: The later operation's closed failures impose no active-principal or granted_projects-scope precondition, so grants may be created for disabled and all-projects principals.
